clue.text: Semites and I chat about sensitivity to beauty

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the preceding words are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Members of two groups chatting about who appreciates beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a devotion to beauty and art, especially the late-Victorian movement of art for art's sake.

clue.text: Space out extremely tedious features

indicators.note: out suggests the word space has its letters thrown out of order
extremely points to the very ends of the word tedious

explanation.surface: A dull set of features spread widely apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SPACE into ASPEC; 'extremely' takes the outside letters of 'tedious', T and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspects and features are synonyms: separate facets or parts of something.

clue.text: Drain small jug

parts.note: a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: An instruction to empty a little jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain and a sewer are both underground channels carrying away waste water.

clue.text: From now on woman's terrible fate is supported by the Queen

indicators.note: in a down entry, being supported means having the next piece placed underneath

parts.note: her is the possessive pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: terrible suggests the word fate is mangled into a different order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword shorthand for the Queen

explanation.surface: A woman's dreadful destiny is propped up by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges FATE into EAFT; 'is supported by' sets ER beneath it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at some later time or henceforth, so it can replace a phrase about the future.

clue.text: Loves to enter motorcycling event and honk horn

indicators.note: to enter means these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
love is zero in tennis, written O, so two loves give OO

explanation.surface: Romance at a motorbike race, with a horn blaring.
explanation.definitionFit: To toot is to sound a car horn with a short blast, which is what honking means.

clue.text: Immigrant: International person of impeccable morals

parts.note: the punctuation mark after the first word is itself a colon, read as a word
a saint, abbreviated ST, is a person of impeccable morals

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style entry describing an immigrant as a global paragon.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation mark is part of the wordplay: the colon after 'Immigrant' supplies its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler arriving in a new territory is a colonist, a kind of immigrant.

clue.text: He broke P Cech's skull in collision

definitions.meaning: Stephen Hunt, the Reading midfielder, fractured goalkeeper Petr Cech's skull in a 2006 match
a minor crash between vehicles, especially one running into the back of another

explanation.surface: A footballer fractured a goalkeeper's skull in a clash.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as S. HUNT, the answer is the footballer's name; the whole word is a slang term for a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A shunt is colloquial for a crash, especially a rear-end impact between cars.

clue.text: Arrange 1,100 drifters

parts.note: to plan something is to arrange it
one thousand is K and one hundred is a ton, so the figure gives K and TON

explanation.surface: Organise a group of eleven hundred wanderers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny organisms that float with ocean currents rather than swimming, hence drifters.

clue.text: Show up bigoted politician ignoring black director

indicators.note: ignoring tells us to leave the following letter out of the name

parts.note: Gerard Batten, a former UKIP leader, was widely criticised for bigoted remarks
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Expose a prejudiced MP while overlooking a black film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show up' looks like 'expose'; it is the definition in its sense of turning up. UKIP was a right-wing British party.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to be present, so to turn up at an event.

clue.text: Tall building with supply leads requiring changing for drill, perhaps

indicators.note: the leads are the opening letters of the two words, which are swapped

parts.note: a tower is a tall building
a pool is a common supply or reserve, as of labour

explanation.surface: Someone describing a skyscraper project that needs new cables, maybe a drill.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric drill is one example of a motor-driven hand tool.

clue.text: Shady individual inspires lecturer

indicators.note: inspires is read literally as breathes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a unit is a single individual thing

explanation.surface: A dubious character motivates a university teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shady' suggests dishonest, but here it means dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Without light, a place is dim or shaded, so shady in the literal sense.

clue.text: Travel buddy is regarding part of the lower arm

definitions.text: regarding part of the lower arm

parts.note: to car is to travel by car, a dated verb
a pal is a friend or buddy

explanation.surface: A companion on a journey turns out to be connected to the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the carpus, the wrist bones between forearm and hand.

clue.text: Metamorphosis of an insect, for example

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a complete transformation, so the letters change shape

explanation.surface: A caterpillar turning into a butterfly is a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' reads as one phrase, but 'for' is a link and 'example' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or illustration of something, hence an example.

clue.text: Perhaps eating cheese mostly provides immunity

indicators.note: eating means one piece swallows the other

parts.note: say is used to mean perhaps or for example

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A diet of cheese may protect you from illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like hedging but gives SAY, as in 'say, ten'.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety is freedom from danger or harm, which is what immunity provides.

clue.text: Ruddy duck is a bird

parts.note: ruddy and flaming are both mild British swearwords meaning bloody
in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, written O

explanation.surface: The ruddy duck is a real species, so the clue claims it is a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy duck' looks like the bird's name, but both words are wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a long-legged pink wading bird.

clue.text: Papers covering very tardy individual

indicators.note: covering means the outer piece goes round the others

parts.note: ID, identity documents, are papers
so means very, as in so good
tardy means late

explanation.surface: Documents protecting someone who is always running late.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated cases are separate, single ones, so the adjective can stand for individual.

clue.text: Blowhard damaged mud hut loo

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters of the following words are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A braggart has wrecked a primitive outdoor toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowhard is a boastful, noisy person, someone who talks too much and too loudly.

clue.text: Propose that trousers neuter when extremely tightly fitting

indicators.note: trousers is read as a verb, to pocket, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to suggest is to propose
N is the grammatical abbreviation for neuter

explanation.surface: Advice that very tight trousers might sterilise the wearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing; it is the verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of snug, meaning most closely fitting, matches the definition's extremely tight.

clue.text: Outrageous old lady that punctured tyre walls

indicators.note: walls is a verb here, meaning surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a flat is a tyre that has been punctured
gran, short for grandmother, is an old lady

explanation.surface: A shocking elderly woman who stabbed a car's tyre sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaringly obvious and shocking, as outrageous behaviour is.

clue.text: Show California's boring flag

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to flag is to weaken or fade
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: Displaying California's dull state banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning wilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is an outward show or false appearance put on for others.

clue.text: How to find pi's root

parts.note: split the entry in two and it is an instruction to turn the letters I and P round, which is how to find pi

explanation.surface: A maths question about finding the root of pi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'root' suggests a square root; it is a root vegetable. 'How to' and 's' just frame the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: This brassica is a root vegetable, grown for its swollen edible root.

clue.text: Planted vegetables outside for cash, once

indicators.note: outside means this piece wraps around the other

parts.note: peas are vegetables
to set seeds or seedlings is to plant them

explanation.surface: Someone grew vegetables in the garden to make some money.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was Spain's currency until the euro replaced it, so it was money in former times.

clue.text: Cheat with drug, receiving sack in game

indicators.note: receiving means the outer letters take in the next piece

parts.note: to crib is to copy or cheat
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: A player cheats using drugs and gets fired mid-game.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored with pegs on a board.

clue.text: Son in ship shot off the side wall

indicators.note: in means this letter goes inside the following piece

parts.note: a boat is a ship

explanation.surface: A boy aboard a vessel is shot from its side.
explanation.definitionFit: In squash, a boast is a stroke played off a side wall before reaching the front.

clue.text: Sergeant Major encounters nettles and grins

parts.note: SM is the military abbreviation for sergeant major
to nettle someone is to annoy or irk them

explanation.surface: An army officer walks into stinging plants and smiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nettles' looks like the plants; it is the verb meaning annoys.
explanation.definitionFit: A smirk is a smug or self-satisfied smile, a kind of grin.

clue.text: Discharge of water from lavatory, say

indicators.note: say indicates that the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a lavatory is a room, as in restroom or the smallest room

explanation.surface: Water leaking from a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is the watery mucus that runs from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Dirty introduction to sex with lubricant

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter, here of sex

parts.note: oil is a lubricant

explanation.surface: A smutty account of starting intercourse with lubricant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty' looks like an adjective; it is the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To soil something is to make it dirty or stain it.

clue.text: In the morning leave Germany, heading west in blind faith

indicators.note: in an across entry heading west means read right to left

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
to go is to leave
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Someone departing Germany early, westward, trusting fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is doctrine accepted without question, hence belief held without evidence.

clue.text: English statue left for leading nationalist as payment

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another, and leading says it is the first one

parts.note: a statue is a monument

explanation.surface: An English statue of a patriot is removed in exchange for money.
explanation.walkthrough: MONUMENT has two Ns; 'leading' says only the first is replaced, giving MOLUMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An emolument is a salary, fee or other remuneration for work.

clue.text: Piles of rubbish in holy mess needing tidying, which takes up energy

indicators.note: in means the rubbish goes inside the rearranged letters
takes up means the rearranged letters absorb the rubbish together with the energy
a mess needing tidying has its letters put into a new order

parts.note: tat is rubbish or junk
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Heaps of junk in a sacred chaos that needs clearing, sapping energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing tidying' rearranges HOLY MESS to S-LYHOMES; TAT and E go inside after the S. A pile is British slang for a grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile is a large imposing building, so grand country houses are piles.
